Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team liked the latency profile and the dedicated pool options. Procurement asked me to pull together the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) but flagged that before they can move to PO we need: a concrete tokens-per-dollar model for our expected traffic shape, documentation on caching/prefetching assumptions, and a short sensitivity table showing the impact of batching/concurrency choices on cost and P50 latency.

To start the MAP we can share traffic targets: 10M monthly requests (mostly API calls from our triage microservice), average prompt+response size ~1,200 tokens, peak burst of ~350 RPS for 90s, and expected steady-state 40 RPS. We have strict SLA needs for <250ms 95th token latency on the critical path.

Can you send a MAP draft that includes: tokens/$ assumptions by model variant, recommended batching and cache TTL defaults (and what tradeoffs those imply), and a quick table of costs under three traffic scenarios (pessimistic/likely/optimistic)? Procurement also needs a single-sheet summary they can attach to the SOW.

I can loop in our procurement lead (procurement@veridianhealth.com) if you need formal docs.

Thanks,
Elena
Product Ops — Veridian Health

Hi Elena — great to connect.

Thanks for the traffic snapshot; that’s exactly what we need to size MAP economics. I’ve attached a short MAP workbook (redwood-map-cost-workbook-v1.xlsx) plus a one-pager (redwood-token-modeling-notes.pdf) that explains our tokens/$ baseline. High-level notes up front:

- Baseline tokens/$: we present two model variants in the workbook: rwd-13b-q4 (recommended for throughput) and rwd-70b-q8 (for higher quality). Baseline tokens-per-dollar in the sheet assume dedicated capacity with steady-state reserved pool; see tab "UnitEcon-Baseline."
- Caching/prefetch: we show both prefix caching (session-based) and intermediate KV cache with a 2-minute TTL default for triage flows — this reduces total token generation by ~22% in the 'likely' scenario. Workbook includes a sensitivity that toggles cache hit rate from 10->50%.
- Batching and concurrency: the sensitivity sheet models three batching profiles: low-latency (max batch 1–4, conservative continuous batching), throughput (max batch 64, aggressive scheduling), and hybrid (max batch 16). Each profile shows tokens/$ and P95 latency delta.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal: we’ll run a quick sensitivity sim for your exact 1,200-token average using your peak/steady RPS numbers.
2) External: we’ll produce a single-page procurement summary for the SOW and a MAP timeline with milestones (pilot -> canary -> GA).

I’ve routed the internal ask below to our ops/infra team — looping in them so they see context. Meeting: can we grab 30m tomorrow to walk the workbook? I can invite Karthik and Ben for the technical walk.

Best,
